# bitwrap.io — Petri nets as ZK containers

bitwrap is a single Go binary (vanilla JS frontend, no npm, no build step)
that treats a Petri net schema as the source of truth for an on-chain
application. From one `.btw` file (or a JSON-LD model saved from the editor)
it generates Solidity contracts, Foundry test suites, Groth16 circuits, and
browser witness builders. The flagship application built this way is
anonymous on-chain voting: every ballot is a Groth16 proof, nobody sees how
you voted, results are sealed while the poll is active, and the final tally
is publicly verifiable.

Hosts: https://bitwrap.io (landing), /poll, /editor, /remix. The subdomains
app.bitwrap.io, api.bitwrap.io, solver.bitwrap.io and prover.bitwrap.io all
reach the same server. All API routes answer CORS preflight and echo the
request `Origin`, so they can be called from any page. Source:
https://github.com/stackdump/bitwrap-io (MIT).

## Voting protocol

1. **Create.** `POST /api/polls` with title, choices, and an EIP-191
   `personal_sign` signature from the creator's Ethereum wallet. No accounts,
   no passwords — the wallet is the identity.
2. **Register.** Voters post a commitment hash to `/api/polls/{id}/register`;
   the server keeps a fixed-depth Merkle registry (`/registry`). The creator
   may sign the registry root (`/sign-registry-root`) to freeze it.
3. **Vote.** The client derives a nullifier as `mimcHash(voterSecret, pollId)`
   (the secret can itself be derived from a wallet signature, so it is
   deterministic per voter per poll), builds a witness with
   `witness-builder.js`, proves `voteCast` in the browser (`prover.js` +
   `prover.wasm`) or via `POST /api/prove`, and posts
   `{nullifier, voteCommitment, proof}` to `/api/polls/{id}/vote`. The
   circuit checks Merkle inclusion in the registry, nullifier binding, and
   vote range; a reused nullifier is rejected without revealing who voted.
4. **Sealed results.** While active, `/api/polls/{id}/results` returns only
   the vote count. Tallies, nullifiers and commitments are withheld so an
   observer cannot diff the tally after each vote and correlate timing to
   de-anonymize voters.
5. **Close.** `POST /api/polls/{id}/close` (creator signature). Afterwards
   `/results`, `/nullifiers`, `/votes` and `/reveal` expose the full audit
   trail; `/tally-proof` (`POST` to generate, `GET` to fetch) carries a proof
   over the final tally.

### v3: homomorphic tally

v3 polls encrypt each ballot under the creator's BabyJubJub public key
(Pedersen/ElGamal-style, `pedersen.js`). Ballot ciphertexts are summed
per-bin without decryption; at close the creator decrypts the aggregate and
proves it with the `tallyDecrypt_8` circuit, then `POST /api/polls/{id}/aggregate`
with `{creator, signature, tallies, decryptProofBytes}`. The tally artifact is
served at `GET /api/polls/{id}/tally`. The `bitwrap close-poll <pollId>`
subcommand does the whole close from the command line:

```sh
bitwrap close-poll <pollId> --sk-hex-file=./creator-bjj.key \
    --eth-key-file=./creator-eth.key --server=https://bitwrap.io
# or BITWRAP_SK_HEX / BITWRAP_ETH_KEY env vars; or --signature=<eip191sig>
# to sign externally in two steps.  --key-dir caches the compiled circuit.
```

## API reference

Polls:

```
POST /api/polls                         Create (wallet signature required)
GET  /api/polls                         List
GET  /api/polls/{id}                    Details
POST /api/polls/{id}/register           Register voter commitment
GET  /api/polls/{id}/registry           Merkle registry
POST /api/polls/{id}/sign-registry-root Creator signs registry root
POST /api/polls/{id}/vote               Cast ZK-proven vote
POST /api/polls/{id}/close              Close (creator signature)
POST /api/polls/{id}/reveal             Reveal a vote choice (post-close)
GET  /api/polls/{id}/results            Results (sealed while active)
GET  /api/polls/{id}/nullifiers         Spent nullifiers
GET  /api/polls/{id}/votes              Per-vote records / v3 ciphertexts
POST /api/polls/{id}/aggregate          v3 close with signed aggregate proof
GET  /api/polls/{id}/tally              v3 tally artifact (post-close)
POST /api/polls/{id}/tally-proof        Generate tally proof
GET  /api/polls/{id}/tally-proof        Fetch tally proof
```

Models and templates:

```
POST /api/save                  Save JSON-LD model -> {"cid": "..."}
GET  /o/{cid}                   Load model (application/ld+json)
GET  /img/{cid}.svg             Render saved model as SVG
POST /api/svg                   Render posted JSON-LD as SVG
GET  /api/templates             List ERC templates (020, 721, 1155, 4626, 5725, vote)
GET  /api/templates/{id}        Full template model (JSON-LD)
```

Code generation (server must run with `-solgen`; enabled on bitwrap.io):

```
POST /api/solgen                Solidity contract from a template/model
POST /api/testgen               Foundry test suite
POST /api/genesisgen            Genesis/deploy script
POST /api/compile               .btw DSL -> schema JSON
GET  /api/bundle/vote           Foundry project ZIP: v1/v2 poll + voteCast verifier
GET  /api/bundle/vote-v3        ZIP: BitwrapZKPollV3 + voteCastHomomorphic_8 +
                                tallyDecrypt_8 verifiers
```

ZK prover:

```
GET  /api/circuits              List compiled Groth16 circuits
POST /api/prove                 Submit a witness, receive a proof
GET  /api/vk/{circuit}          Verifying key (binary)
GET  /api/vk/{circuit}/solidity Solidity verifier contract (text/plain)
GET  /api/keys/{circuit}        Proving key material (binary)
```

Other: `GET /metrics` (Prometheus). `POST /api/dev/sign` exists for local
development wallets only.

## Model format

Models saved from the editor are JSON-LD with `@context: https://pflow.xyz/schema`
— the same format as pflow.xyz (`places` and `transitions` keyed by id, `arcs`
as `{source, target, weight}` with vector weights per token color). The CID
returned by `/api/save` is computed from the URDNA2015-canonicalized document
(CIDv1, sha256); `seal-cid.mjs` reproduces it in the browser and the Go
sealer (`internal/seal`) is the reference. `/o/{cid}` serves the document
back unchanged.

## The .btw DSL

`.btw` is a compact schema language for Petri net state machines. Registers
are places (optionally keyed maps), `fn(...)` blocks are transitions, arrows
`-|weight|>` are arcs, `require(...)` lines are guards, `@event` emits a
Solidity event, and `requires <role>` binds a caller role.

```
schema Poll {
  version "1.0"
  register nullifiers map[uint256]bool observable
  register tallies map[uint256]uint256 observable
  event VoteCast { nullifier: uint256 indexed  choice: uint256 }
  fn(castVote) {
    var nullifier uint256
    var choice uint256
    var weight uint256
    require(nullifiers[nullifier] == false)
    @event VoteCast
    castVote -|weight|> tallies
    castVote -|weight|> nullifiers
  }
}
```

`bitwrap -compile poll.btw` emits schema JSON (same as `POST /api/compile`);
`bitwrap -synthesize examples/erc20.btw` emits gnark circuit source;
`bitwrap -validate` runs the end-to-end deploy pipeline (needs Foundry's
`forge` + `anvil`).

## Circuit synthesis

There is no hand-written gnark code in the repo. `prover/synth` maps schema
primitives onto Groth16 constraints:

| Petri net primitive                    | Circuit constraint                      |
|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| keyed input arc `BALANCES[from] -|n|>` | Merkle membership proof in pre-state    |
| keyed output arc `-|n|> BALANCES[to]`  | post-state commitment hash              |
| guard `BALANCES[from] >= n`            | range check via `ToBinary`              |
| role `fn(mint) requires minter`        | `caller == minter` equality             |
| ZKOp nullifier-bind / commitment-bind  | MiMC / Keccak derivation constraint     |

Generated circuits: transfer, mint, burn, approve, transferFrom, vestClaim,
voteCast (v1/v2), plus voteCastHomomorphic_8 and tallyDecrypt_8 (v3). Each is
a `frontend.Circuit` with public/private partitioning and Merkle arrays sized
per `State.MerkleDepth`. The verifying key and the Solidity verifier are
produced together, so on-chain verification matches off-chain proving
byte-for-byte. CI runs `make gen-circuits && git diff --exit-code` to catch
stale output.

## Client modules

All are dependency-free ES modules served from https://bitwrap.io/ (CORS-open)
and mirrored at `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/stackdump/bitwrap-io@<tag>/public/<file>`.

```html
<script type="module">
import { mimcHash } from "https://bitwrap.io/mimc.js";
import { MerkleTree } from "https://bitwrap.io/merkle.js";
import { buildVoteCastWitness } from "https://bitwrap.io/witness-builder.js";
</script>
```

- `mimc.js` — MiMC-BN254 hash, pure BigInt.
- `merkle.js` — fixed-depth binary Merkle tree with inclusion proofs.
- `witness-builder.js` — witness builders for every generated circuit.
- `pedersen.js` — BabyJubJub Pedersen commitments for v3 ballots.
- `prover.js` / `prover-worker.js` / `prover.wasm` — Groth16 proving in a
  Web Worker (the Go prover cross-compiled to wasm; `wasm_exec.js` runtime).
- `seal-cid.mjs` — JSON-LD canonicalization + CID, parity-tested against Go.
- `petri-view.js`, `petri-view.css`, `petri-sim.js`, `petri-solver.js`,
  `petri-colors.js` — vendored copies of the pflow.xyz browser modules, pinned
  by hash (`pflow-js.lock`) and by version (Bazel `git_override`). For the
  editor/simulator/ODE API, read https://pflow.xyz/llms-full.txt; bugs in
  these files are fixed in pflow-xyz and synced here.

Go <-> JS parity (MiMC, Pedersen, witness layout, CID, type coercion) is
enforced by `.mjs` tests under `public/` that run in CI and under Bazel.

## Running locally

```sh
git clone https://github.com/stackdump/bitwrap-io && cd bitwrap-io
make run          # :8088 ; flags: -port -data -solgen -compile -synthesize -validate
make test         # Go tests + vendored-JS hash check
```

Go >= 1.24. Foundry only for `make validate`; npm only for the Playwright e2e
suite. Polls, votes and events are stored on the filesystem under `-data`.
